lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
If anyone heads for Deep Dark, tell them. Walk soft and do not open every chest.
Sculk hears what pride forgets.
The part about a wool-lined chamber off the main path is what makes that story from Deep Dark feel real to me.
I'll remember Deep Dark as darkness that listens back.
Across the sculk-lined passages of Deep Dark, I'd keep everyone close enough to hear a warning.
Hooves find trouble before eyes sometimes, especially around the sculk-lined passages of Deep Dark.
I had heard of {target}, but your description of a buried cavern where silence matters more than light makes the journey sound rough.
I would drop every bag before leaving someone alone with a warden rising from the darkness.
Anyone facing the warden, shriekers, and one noisy mistake needs a plan for the first mistake.
A heavy pack is no use if a friend needs help across the sculk-lined passages of Deep Dark.
My pack would hold wool, food, and no loose gear rattling in the dark before I went anywhere near a buried cavern where silence matters more than light.
I would keep one person awake at a wool-lined chamber off the main path while the others recovered.
We would not leave the wool markers leading upward until the next safe point was clear.
Did any route keep you clear of the warden, shriekers, and one noisy mistake?
The thought of a single sound waking the sculk would have me checking the ground every few steps.
Every stop near Deep Dark should end with names called and answers heard.
I would not move on until I trusted a wool path that leads straight back out.
A journey around a buried cavern where silence matters more than light can outlast a food bag. Did yours?
I could not stop worrying about the warden, shriekers, and one noisy mistake before you returned.
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below.
If anyone heads for Dripstone Caves, tell them. Look up as often as you look down.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious.
That tale makes Dripstone Caves feel much closer than it did a moment ago.
I will remember Dripstone Caves as a cave that bites from both directions.
I would not argue over packs with a zombie moving beyond the torchlight nearby.
I would notice ears and hooves first if stalactites above and spikes below were near.
After a trip near a cavern lined with stone points above and below, rounding up a loose lamb sounds peaceful.
I would put a calm traveler beside anyone frightened by stalactites above and spikes below.
Would you have found home without a broad ledge marked before climbing deeper?
I bet the first village fence was a welcome sight after a cavern lined with stone points above and below.
I'd keep a shorter line and use louder voices across the pointed passages of Dripstone Caves.
No treasure could make me ignore falling dripstone, narrow ledges, and deep holes.
Everyone gets water and a quiet minute at a flat chamber clear of dripstone. That would be my rule.
After leaving behind a cavern lined with stone points above and below, even our muddy sheepfold must have looked welcoming.
I would mark the torch trail toward the entrance where everyone could see it.
I can do without copper and stone gathered away from the sharpest ground if getting it means taking that road.
The risk of stalactites above and spikes below deserves more thought than whatever treasure drew us there.
Spare cloth can warm a traveler, mark a route, or cover a wound near Dripstone Caves.
You described water tapping from one stone point to another so clearly that I nearly felt I was there.
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
If anyone heads for Lush Caves, tell them. Watch the vines and the holes between them.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe.
The part about a dry ledge beside a mossy wall is what makes that story from Lush Caves feel real to me.
I will remember Lush Caves as a cave trying very hard to look harmless.
Hooves find trouble before eyes sometimes, especially around the vine-filled chambers of Lush Caves.
I can see why you went after clay, glow berries, and moss from safe ledges, but that was a hard road.
Nobody should cross the vine-filled chambers of Lush Caves alone after hearing that story.
You found your way home after seeing an underground garden hanging over dark pools. That is the part I like best.
I would pause at the rooted dirt trail leading upward and point out the return path.
Give me a quiet pasture instead of an underground garden hanging over dark pools any time.
One glimpse of a zombie climbing through the vines would be enough. We would leave together.
I bet the ordinary road home felt kind after an underground garden hanging over dark pools.
Did you set up a route following solid stone instead of hanging vines before exploring, or only when it was time to leave?
I'd make sure everyone understood glow berries hiding deep drops before we left.
I would keep picturing glow berries shining above dripping leaves for days.
I would make a dry ledge beside a mossy wall our meeting place if the route forced us apart.
After hearing about Lush Caves, I believe this. A shepherd knows the value of a warm layer when a journey lasts longer than planned.
If I ran into hidden drops, axolotls underfoot, and vines over open space, I would turn around.
The strongest walkers should carry supper, not just whatever looked valuable at Lush Caves.
